description:
Research Summary

This Liverpool–AFBI studentship investigates metabolic responses to methane-suppressing feed additives in beef cattle.

It is advertised for UK students who meet the stated eligibility requirements.

Official Project Title

Livestock Metabolomics: Investigating Metabolic Signatures of Methane Mitigation in Beef Cattle

Research Focus and Methods

Profile biological samples across the production cycle and integrate metabolomics with methane emissions, microbiome information and animal performance. Investigate biomarkers associated with mitigation, health and feed efficiency.

Research Training and Development

Research includes field and laboratory work at AFBI in Northern Ireland and metabolomics analysis at Liverpool.

Funding and Duration

Studentship funding and award conditions
ComponentDetails

ProgrammeAFBI-funded studentship

StipendA living stipend is funded for four years; the advert does not publish a numeric annual rate.
Tuition and research supportAFBI funds tuition fees and a four-year stipend, provided eligibility is met.
Award conditionsSelection is competitive; an advertised project does not guarantee a studentship.

Eligibility and English Language

Applicant qualifications and funding eligibility
ComponentDetails
Applicant eligibilityUK students meeting the advert’s eligibility rules; applicants from Northern Ireland and the island of Ireland are encouraged to apply subject to those rules.
Academic preparationAt least a 2:1-equivalent honours degree in Animal Science, Chemistry, Biology, Biochemistry or a related biological discipline.
Project interests and skillsInterest in animal research, mass spectrometry and quantitative biological analysis.
English languageMeet the host university’s English-language admission rules. An approved alternative or exemption may apply; IELTS is not universally mandatory.

Application Dates and Location

Deadline, start date and research location

How to Apply

  1. Email Dr Howbeer Muhamadali and Dr Seyed Ali Goldansaz using the official advert’s addresses.
  2. Include your CV, cover letter, a relevant research proposal of no more than two pages and two reference letters.
  3. Follow the university’s subsequent online application instructions.

Application Checklist

  • CV
  • Cover letter
  • Relevant research proposal, maximum two pages
  • Two reference letters covering academic potential and professional suitability
